description: Greeny Space is a team focused on using NASA satellite data, Google Earth Engine, and modern technology to support sustainable agriculture. Our project, Greeny Farms, aims to monitor crop health, analyze vegetation using NDVI, and visualize farmland through satellite imagery. We want to help farmers understand vegetation conditions, identify areas that may need attention, and make better agricultural decisions. Our mission is to promote smart farming, environmental sustainability,greener future.
summary: GreenySpace is a farmer-centred decision-support concept developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Field Shift challenge. It aims to help farmers understand climate conditions and explore better crop-rotation choices by combining NASA Earth observation data with local farm information such as soil condition, crop history and water availability. The proposed platform includes a mobile-friendly dashboard, a Crop Rotation Explorer and an AI-assisted Crop Doctor concept. It is designed to make complex environmental information easier for farmers to understand. Our goal is to support climate-aware farm planning while keeping farmers and agricultural experts involved in important decisions.
details: GreenySpace is designed to support farmers in adapting to changing climate conditions. The proposed system combines NASA climate and Earth observation information with farm-level details such as location, soil condition, crop history and water availability. Main proposed modules: 1. NASA Data Centre: To access and present climate information for a selected farm location. 2. Crop Rotation Explorer: To compare the current crop sequence with alternative crop-rotation options. 3. AI Crop Doctor: To explain possible climate and crop risks using available information. 4. Farm Dashboard: To present farm information in a simple mobile-friendly interface. 5. Future Polyhouse Monitoring: To support climate monitoring and, after hardware testing, safe ventilation automation. The project is being developed using a web-based application approach. The team is exploring NASA POWER and other relevant NASA resources for climate information. Our aim is to make climate information easier to understand and help farmers explore informed crop-planning decisions. The system is a decision-support concept and does not replace agricultural experts. Current limitations: NASA data integration, live sensor connectivity, AI validation and automatic polyhouse control must be tested before being described as operational features.
